powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_1: Place a hanger directly above the rail. It can also sit partway through a curve or climb.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_2: After linking, the crossbeam turns across the track. Add hangers along bends and climbs to support both wires.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_3: Right-click with an empty hand to change the width. The default opening is 7 blocks wide.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_4: Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to set the wire height. Leave room for the train and the roof pickup.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_1: Hold Power Grid Copper Wire and sneak-right-click the first hanger.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_2: Sneak-right-click the next hanger to preview both paths. Sneak-right-click it again to confirm.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_3: At a fork, sneak-right-click a rail on the branch you want. Link back to an existing hanger to close a loop.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_4: Wire Power Grid to the copper posts on any hanger. Several supplies can feed the same line.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_5: Sneak-right-click the rail with an empty hand. Highlight one span in the hanger settings, then confirm the cut.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_1: Mount the pantograph along the carriage and connect its two posts to the onboard circuit.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_2: Right-click with an empty hand to raise it. The contact bar follows both overhead wires.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_3: At an insulated gap, the head stays raised while the onboard circuit disconnects.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_4: The pickup reconnects automatically under the next powered section.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_5: Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to open the receiver. Match both item slots to the cab's transmitting Redstone Link.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_6: Turn the cab signal on to raise the pickup from inside the train.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_7: Turn the signal off to lower it and disconnect power.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_1: Mount facing Power Docks on two Sable craft, or put one on a fixed station.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_2: Wire Positive and Negative into the local circuit on each side. The docks join matching posts in parallel.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_3: Arm both docks with redstone and bring the craft together slowly.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_4: As the heads meet, the amber lamps light. Power can flow either way and a comparator reads 15.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_5: Turn off either dock to open the circuit, retract the arms, and release that pair.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_1: Mount the Deck Rail Jumper on an open Loconautics deck. Point the cord outlet at the next car.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_2: Match the outlet to a knuckle that faces the same way. Corner mounts work when the next car has a matching jumper.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_3: Wire the two copper posts on top to the car's Power Grid circuit. Keep Positive and Negative matched.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_4: With CC: Tweaked, place a Networking Cable directly above the socket to join the cars' wired networks.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_5: When the knuckles couple, the cord connects power and optional data. The amber lamp shows the connection.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_6: The cord flexes as the coupled cars turn and climb.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_7: Uncouple the knuckles to retract the cord and disconnect both circuits.
powerdock.ponder.flush_rail_jumper.text_: Fit the Flush Rail Jumper into a Loconautics end wall. Install it from inside, facing the next car.
Match the outlet to a knuckle that faces the same way. Corner mounts work when the next car has a matching jumper.
Wire both copper posts from inside the car. The power posts and the square data socket share the inside face.
With CC: Tweaked, put a Networking Cable directly against the inside socket. The cord comes out on the other side of the wall.
When the knuckles couple, the cord connects power and optional data. The amber lamp shows the connection.
The cord flexes as the coupled cars turn and climb.
Uncouple the knuckles to retract the cord and disconnect both circuits.
